articleTitle: Lightweight fast target detection method based on YOLOv5
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of a kind of video surveillance bayonet, such as relatively fixed and simple scene size, slow target movement speed and single target category, a lightweight fast target detection method based on YOLOv5 is proposed to meet the hardware requirements of embedded monitoring equipment for simple and fast algorithm. Firstly, the network compression of YOLOv5 model is carried out, and a lightweight network YOLOv5-tiny is proposed, which reduces the network complexity, reduces the memory occupation and improves the detection speed. At the same time, in order to make up for the accuracy loss caused by network compression, a lightweight attention module is introduced into the network to improve the detection accuracy. In the COCO dataset, mAP50 and mAP reached 44.7% and 26.4% respectively, and FPS was 370 frames / s. In the VOC dataset, mAP50 decreased by only 2.1% and reached 76.4% compared with the network before compression. In addition, the GPU utilization rate in model reasoning is only 949MB, which is greatly improved compared with other lightweight networks, and fully meets the practical application requirements in embedded monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Anti-disturbance tracking control for the nonlinear system with state cascade extended state observer under disturbance
abstract: The anti-disturbance tracking control of a class of nonlinear systems that is subject to time-varying disturbance is researched in this paper. To restrain the effect of the disturbance on the state tracking of the nonlinear system, a state cascade extended state observer (SCESO) is designed. Then, based on the disturbance estimation obtained from the SCESO, the controller is designed. Combined with the Hurwitz matrix and the Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions of the resulting closed-loop system are given. Finally, the performance of the designed control strategy is verified by the comparative simulation.

articleTitle: Dual-component inter-dependent failure mechanism analysis of diesel engine based on counterfactual inference
abstract: For diesel engines, the coupling between the high-pressure oil pump and injector complicates fault diagnosis, and relationships between faults and symptoms are complex. Without analyzing inter-dependent failure mechanisms, it is straightforward to fall into the trap of pseudo-relevance with big data and there is also no guarantee of the accuracy and robustness of the predictive model. Multi-facto accidents are characterized by strong concealment, complex factor association, irreversible state, etc. Analyzing inter-dependent failure mechanisms remains a challenging problem in the reliability and safety of diesel engines. To address these challenges, this paper constructs a dual-component inter-dependent failure mechanism analysis method. First, a fault causal network is constructed using domain knowledge. Next, the Leaky Noisy-Or assumption and hidden variable nodes are incorporated to establish a Structural Causal Model (SCM). In addition, counterfactual inference based on do operator intervention in twin networks is employed to calculate two metrics: expected sufficiency and expected disablement, measuring the strength of the causal explanation of faults on the symptom. Finally, the case study demonstrates that this method effectively provides a clear causal chain of failure and intuitively reveals the causal relationship between fault causes and fault symptoms.

articleTitle: Multi-unmanned ground vehicle formation and motion planning based on graph and fluid disturbance algorithm under external disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the formation motion planning for multiple unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in a complex environment with moving threats and static obstacles. To this end, a formation motion planning algorithm based on rigid graph theory and fluid disturbance algorithm is designed. First, aiming at the formation control problem under external disturbances, the graph theory is applied to describe the cooperative relationship between multiple UGVs. Then, considering the distance constraints between UGVs, a leader-follower formation controller is designed based on the backstepping method. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the convergence of the proposed control method can be guaranteed. Furthermore, aiming at the formation motion planning of the UGVs under complex dynamic environments, a motion planning approach is developed by resorting to the fluid disturbance algorithm, in which the leader UGV plans the overall trajectory of the formation system, and realizes the obstacle avoidance of the UGV formation systems. Finally, numerical simulations are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A dispatch strategy for microgrid considering the benefits of electric vehicle demand response
abstract: With the large-scale operation of electric vehicles in the network, how to realize the rational planning of the output of each distributed power supply under the premise of the lowest comprehensive cost is of great significance. The charging load of electric vehicles predicted by Monte Carlo sampling method reflects that if the charging load of electric vehicles is not guided, it will cause the peak of micro-electric power load. Therefore, this paper proposes a microgrid optimization scheduling strategy based on Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) for orderly charging and discharging of electric vehicles. Under the guidance of the time-of-use tariff mechanism, electric vehicles achieve orderly charging and discharging that takes into account economy and demand response. Finally, the Improved Grey Wolf optimization (IGWO) algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. The example analysis shows that the proposed orderly charge and discharge strategy not only realizes the peak cutting and valley filling of power load, but also significantly reduces the economic operation cost and environmen tal protection cost of microgrid.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a bilateral oscillating magnetic-adhesion wall-climbing inspection robot
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of damage detection and weld inspection on large pipeline wall surfaces, as well as to improve the obstacle-surmounting capabilities of wall-climbing robots, a new pipeline wall-climbing inspection robot is proposed. This paper introduces a bilateral oscillating magnetic-adhesion wall-climbing inspection robot and designs an automated TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction) flaw detection mechanism. Subsequently, a static analysis model and kinematic analysis of the robot are established. Finally, an experimental platform and prototype are constructed, and field tests are conducted on spherical tanks. The experiments demonstrate that the robot can move flexibly and stably on curved wall surfaces, completing damage detection and weld inspection following standard procedures.

articleTitle: Fixed-time stable composite control of the hybrid mechanism with time-varying mismatched disturbance
abstract: For the hybrid mechanism is affected by the time-varying matched/mismatched disturbances in the operation process, the fixed-time stable composite control method is proposed for the hybrid mechanism with time-varying mismatched disturbance. Firstly, the estimations of time-varying mismatched disturbance and its derivative are achieved by the generalized proportional-integral observer with uniform bandwidth parameters to extend the time-varying mismatched disturbance and its derivative into system states and establish the extended state-space model; Secondly, the fixed-time stable composite control algorithm for hybrid mechanism is designed by combining the estimations of time-varying mismatched disturbance and its derivative to simultaneously suppress the time-varying matched/mismatched disturbances and improve the robustness of the system. Based on the fixed-time Lyapunov stability theory, the fixed-time stability of the designed control algorithm is proved. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control method is verified by simulation experiments and prototype experiments of the hybrid mechanism system used for automobile electro-coating conveying.

articleTitle: Robust velocity-regulation control of gimbal servo systems using a predictive comprehensive disturbance observer
abstract: A robust high-precision velocity-regulation controller is researched for gimbal servo systems (GSSs) in this paper, which aims to mitigate the impact of multiple adverse factors, including both the internal time-delay characteristics and external time-varying disturbances. First, to enable a more accurate estimation and compensation against disturbances of multifrequency-band under input time-delay, a generalized system modelling of GSS is developed with detailed classification and description of different uncertainties. On the basis of such a generalized model, a predictive comprehensive disturbance observer (PCDO) is designed to accurately predict both system states and multiple disturbances with multi-frequency-band. Based upon the predictions provided from PCDO, a composite controller is further constructed to ensure the closed-loop stability of GSS. A rigorous robust stability proof of the closed-loop system is presented. Simulation analysis under various uncertainties are conducted to thoroughly validate the efficacy of the proposed PCDO-based control approach.

articleTitle: Collaborative path planning based on improved ACO for multiple UAV coverage operations
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of multi-UAV full-coverage cooperative operation, the concave polygon decomposition method is adopted to decompose the concave polygon into multiple convex polygons, and then the scanline-based convex polygon operation path generation algorithm is utilized to determine the total operation paths of the co ncave polygons. An improved ant colony algorithm is proposed, which adopts a competitive mechanism to make all path nodes assigned to each UAV, realizes the multiple ants parallel strategy by improving the structure of the shared taboo table, and comprehen sively considers the length of the UAV transfer paths and the mission balance index for the operation path planning. The pheromone update introduces the total operation path length and mission balance index to realize the cooperative optimization of multi-UAV full-coverage operation path planning, and the effectiveness of the modified algorithm is verified through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Topology identification of weighted general complex dynamical networks with saturated inputs
abstract: As is known to all, the topology of network plays an important role in determining a network’s dynamics and function. In this paper, the topology identification problem of weighted general complex dynamical networks with saturated inputs is addressed. First, we establish an original network and design a saturation function to describe a simple nonlinear phenomenon of saturated-input. Then an observer network with the same number of nodes and node dynamics as the original network is designed, using the state errors between the original network and the observer network as feedback. Second, based on the Lyapunov stability theory and LaSalle’s invariance principle, an adaptive saturation identification controller is designed, and the topology of the original network is successfully identified by constructing a drive-response network. Finally, some numerical simulations are developed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Motion planning for mobile robots based on improved artificial potential field algorithm
abstract: The artificial potential field approach has been extensively utilized in autonomous robot path planning, primarily due to its straightforward mathematical formulation. However, much of the research to date has concentrated on static environments, where neither the goal nor obstacles exhibit movement. This paper introduces an improved artificial potential field algorithm designed for dynamic environments by incorporating rotational vector. The proposed approach employs attractive forces to steer the robot towards its goal, while rotational repulsion mechanisms ensure effective obstacle avoidance when dealing with moving objects. Simulation outcomes demonstrate the efficacy of the enhanced method in dynamic scenarios.

articleTitle: Cable inspection robot based on adaptive adjustment elastic damping suspensions
abstract: As the core component of cable-stayed and suspension bridges, the condition of cables is directly related to the safety and reliability of the whole bridge. Therefore, it is particularly important to maintain and inspect the cables regularly. In order to improve the efficiency of cable inspection work, we propose a new wheeled cable inspection robot. The robot adopts a bilateral wheel structure, which consists of four independent suspension mechanisms, and realises the functions of cable installation, attachment, climbing and obstacle-crossing by cooperating with the lifting mechanism. This design provides the robot with greater flexibility and adaptability, enabling it to operate stably in complex cable environments. The robot is powered by the lithium battery it carries, and ground personnel can operate it remotely via a wireless control system, ensuring the safety and convenience of the inspection work. In this paper, we provide a detailed introduction to the structural principle of the robot, especially the suspension mechanism for in-depth kinematic analysis and simulation studies, the simulation results verify the functionality and reliability of the suspension mechanism, this new wheeled cable inspection robot provides an efficient and reliable method for the maintenance and inspection of cables.

articleTitle: Topology-guided multi-view clustering via witness complex
abstract: Despite recent empirical successes in multi-view clustering, several challenges persist. In practical scenarios, data often originate from diverse perspectives or sources, leading to missing data and alignment issues. To overcome such challenges, we propose a novel multi-view clustering framework, termed Topology-Guided Multi-view Clustering via Witness Complex (TGMC-WC). A witness complex is a particular type of complex utilized for extracting topological features. TGMC-WC, from the perspective of addressing erroneous sample pairs, mitigates the impact of false negative pairs by jointly considering topological structures and contrastive learning constraints. Subsequently, we employ contrastive learning to minimize the distance between similar samples. Extensive experiments on datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Collision-free and efficient robotic grasping based on hierarchical reinforcement learning
abstract: In the realm of robotics, grasping within unstructured environments has consistently been a challenging task. Direct grasping often results in failures due to collisions, and some pre-grasping maneuvers can eliminate the tightly stacked state between objects, thereby enhancing the success rate of grasping. In this paper, we opt for pushing as a pre-grasping maneuver. We propose a deep Q-network with a fused convolutional feature enhancement module to improve action value estimation, enhancing the robot’s pushing and grasping abilities. Additionally, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework optimizes action sequences for better synergy between pushing and grasping. In simulated experiments, the model achieved a high grasp success rate with just a few hours of training, outperforming other methods in the literature.

articleTitle: A multi-task assignment algorithm for UAV cluster collaborative emergence based on iterative MILP
abstract: In this paper, an iterative mixed integer linear programming (MILP) algorithm based on the traditional MILP algorithm is proposed to realize the multi-task assignment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) cluster collaborative emergence. This algorithm uses iteration and prediction method to avoid the defect of traditional MILP algorithm that requires scene update to carry out the next calculation, and by using the current task assignment result to carry out the next prediction, the information utilization degree is improved, and the real-time performance is greatly improved. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed iterative MILP algorithm has better real-time and collaborative emergence characteristics than the traditional MILP algorithm.

articleTitle: An effective UWB/IMU joint positioning based on improved anti-NLoS adaptive extended Kalman filter
abstract: In order to solve the problem that Ultra Wide Band (UWB) is susceptible to Non Line of Sight (NLoS) and the demand for high-precision positioning of UAV in indoor warehouse occlusion scenarios, this paper proposes a UWB/IMU joint positioning algorithm based on improved anti-NLoS adaptive extended Kalman filter. The algorithm improves the anti-NLoS discriminant correction algorithm based on the residual threshold and the IMU self-correction algorithm, and combines the data fusion characteristics of the extended Kalman filter for fusion positioning. The initial positioning value and the corrected ranging value are obtained, which are used as the initial values of the Taylor algorithm to get optimal positioning value. Experimental results show that the proposed method can inhibit the influence of NLoS, effectively improve the positioning accuracy and stability. It is effectively applied to UAV flight positioning and trajectory planning in indoor warehouse.

articleTitle: Research on prediction of cucumber growth environment in greenhouse based on IPSO-BP algorithm
abstract: Conventional BP neural networks and PSO-BP neural networks have problems such as insuﬀicient prediction accuracy and weak generalization ability in agricultural greenhouse prediction models. This paper introduces the adaptive weight factor in the PSO-BP neural network. First, select representative relevant features as input parameters for the prediction model and preprocess the sample data; then, an IPSO-BP greenhouse prediction model is constructed by combining the principles of conventional BP and PSO-BP; Finally, the IPSO-BP model is trained, and the prediction results are output. The prediction results show that the IPSO-BP model achieved a coeﬀicient of determination (R²) of 0.92827 for temperature prediction in agricultural greenhouses, with RMSE, MAE, and MRE values of 0.48141, 0.32311, and 1.477%, respectively. For humidity prediction, the IPSO-BP model reached an R² of 0.93405, with RMSE, MAE, and MRE values of 2.4661, 1.7145, and 2.3442%, respectively. These results are superior to those of conventional BP and PSO-BP prediction models.

articleTitle: MP-Prompt:multi-granularity prompt for continual learning
abstract: Continual learning aims to enable model to learn new task sequentially without forgetting previously learned task knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel method called multi-granularity prompt for continual learning (MP-Prompt) with vision transformer. MP-Prompt leverages the global information of the task sequence, task-specific knowledge, and instance-level details to generate multi-granularity prompt. This prompt effectively guide the pre-trained model to learn new tasks while preserving the information acquired from previous tasks. However, existing approaches that focus mainly on local information and fail to fully exploit knowledge at different levels of the task sequence. Therefore, MP-Prompt provide a more comprehensive framework, effectively improving the model ability to handle sequential task. Experiments on benchmark datasets Cifar 100 and ImageNet-R demonstrate that MP-Prompt outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. The results show that MP-Prompt effectively learns new tasks without relying on a rehearsal buffer, significantly mitigating catastrophic forgetting. This approach enhances both the model’s plasticity and stability.

articleTitle: Single-factor multi-level fermentation model based on linear parameter varying finite impulse response
abstract: The fermentation process of Corynebacterium glutamicum exhibits complex dynamic characteristics such as nonlinearity and strong coupling, which makes it difficult to establish an accurate dynamic model, thus making the system challenging to optimize and control. Considering nonlinear dynamic processes can be well described by Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) models, this work suggests a method for modeling the Corynebacterium glutamicum fermentation process based on Linear Parameter Varying Finite Impulse Response (LPV-FIR). Three product (succinic, lactic, and acetic) concentrations and their dynamic interactions with the oxygen transfer coefficient (KLA) are described. Experiments prove that this model can describe the dynamic changes of all the variables in the fermentation process, which has a certain accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Double wavelet threshold filter design for real-time adaptive denoising in OA-ICOS
abstract: In the Off-Axis Integrated Cavity Output Spectroscopy (OA-ICOS) technique, single-stage filters are commonly used to reduce noise and improve the signal-to-noise ratio, enabling more precise CO2 concentration detection. However, these filters often underperform under real-time conditions. To enhance real-time performance, this paper proposes a novel framework based on Double Wavelet Threshold Filter (DWTF) that adaptively suppresses noise while preserving key features of CO2 concentration signal. Firstly, one wavelet threshold filter (WT) is introduced to calculate the mean of the current sequence, providing an initial denoising step. Secondly, another WT is employed to extract features from a longer sequence for adaptive computation of the discount factor. Finally, an exponential moving average filter (EMA) is applied to combine both current and historical data to produce a smoother aggregated output. To validate the effectiveness, DWTF was compared with other conventional algorithms for a CO2 dataset with three distinct states: smooth, ship and mutant, obtained by OA-ICOS. The experimental results demonstrate that DWTF performs effectively in all three states.

articleTitle: Data-driven model-free adaptive control for platooning systems with dual-channel event-triggered mechanism
abstract: This paper studies a model-free adaptive control problem for a platooning system with limited communication resources. Firstly, a redefined output is defined for the platooning system to satisfy the quasi-linear assumption in model-free adaptive control theory. Based on redefined output and input data, we establish a linear data model for the platooning system. Subsequently, a pseudo-partial derivative estimator is designed, and a dual-channel event-triggered scheme is developed to reduce network communication resources. Then, a model-free adaptive controller based on the dual-channel event-triggered scheme is designed. Finally, the convergence of the designed method is strictly proved, and its effectiveness is verified through simulation studies.

articleTitle: DAC-SaNet: improved skip connections in U-Net for medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a pivotal role in various domains, including biomedical research, clinical diagnosis, and pathological analysis. Nevertheless, the prevalent U-shaped network architecture in current medical image segmentation suffers from limitations such as inadequate fusion of hierarchical feature information through simplistic concatenation and the ineﬀiciency of all skip connections. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight DAC-SaNet framework, designed to mitigate the unequal contribution of skip connections, semantic gap, and connectivity constraints in traditional U-nets. Specifically, our framework incorporates a Spatial Channel Attention Fusion Module with Dilated Convolutions(SAFD), enhancing feature extraction across multiple spatial scales to bolster the model’s adaptability and recognition capabilities for diverse scale features in images. Additionally, a Dual Attention Fusion Channel Shuffle Module(DACS) is introduced to capture global dependencies within feature maps, fostering learnable and robust connections between the encoder and decoder. Experimental results demonstrate that our network achieves accuracy of 88.57%, 94.52%, and 74.75% on the ISBI, DSB2018, and the Esophagus and Esophageal Cancer dataset from the First Aﬀiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art models(unet,unet++.attentionunet) with fewer parameters and superior evaluation scores. Our research contributes to advancing the frontier of medical image segmentation.

articleTitle: Research on sign language recognition based on attention mechanism
abstract: Sign language recognition technology can break the communication disorder between the hearing impaired and the able- bodied because the able-bodied cannot understand sign language, which is of great significance to help the hearing impaired integrate into the life of normal people. This article proposes an attention mechanism to improve the model’s feature extraction ability for sign language recognition of isolated words, and a solution to enhance the model’s context connection ability for sign language recognition of continuous sentences by combining attention mechanism with Seq2Seq framework. We have built an isolated word sign language recognition model based on Resnet+BLSTM+Attention, an isolated word sign language recognition model based on Video Swin Transformer, and a continuous statement sign language recognition model based on Seq2Seq+Attention. Experimental verification was conducted on the CLS-500 dataset, and the experimental results showed that selective attention to temporal features through attention mechanism effectively improved recognition accuracy. The accuracy of Video Swin Transformer based on spatio-temporal attention mechanism is much higher than the commonly used sign language recognition methods. The Seq2Seq framework enhances the model’s contextual connection ability and completes the recognition task of continuous sentences well, Verified the excellent performance of the attention mechanism and the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Quality inspection method for splicing welds of PHC piles based on line structured light
abstract: The accuracy of extracting the centerline of weld seam laser directly affects the accuracy of weld seam inspection detec- tion. However, in practical conditions, due to significant surface undulations of PHC piles, reflections on the construction site, and insufficient laser power, existing algorithms are easily affected by noise . To address these issues, this paper proposes a method combining an internally advanced gray centroid method to extract the initial center point. To meet industrial measurement accuracy requirements, principal component analysis is used to solve the normal of the initial center point, and secondary optimization of the center point is performed along the normal direction. Feature point extraction algorithms are integrated to detect feature points of the weld seam laser stripes, which are then transformed into the camera coordinate system for weld seam formation quality detection. Experimental results show that, compared to manual measurement, this method offers higher accuracy and shorter time consumption, meeting the real-time requirements of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Research of crane scheduling in coil yard
abstract: The optimization of crane scheduling in the steel coil yard is a key guarantee for the continuous operation of downstream production lines. Traditional crane scheduling relies on manual experience and has significant limitations. To reduce the workload of workers and improve the production efficiency of steel enterprises, a crane scheduling model integrating loading and stacking was established. With the fastest completion time as the optimization objective, a scheduling strategy with master- slave optimization and dynamic programming is proposed. The strategy substantially reduces the redundant computation while eliminating the inferior solutions, thus obtaining an extremely fast solution speed. As verified by the simulation platform, the strategy reduces the consumed time by 24%-28% compared to a simulation-based genetic algorithm. To test the application feasibility of the algorithm, the method was applied to a certain steel enterprise. The application results indicate that this method can basically meet the downstream production rhythm, which is of great significance for steel enterprises to achieve unmanned and automated production, and has high practical value.

articleTitle: Shape-guided industrial anomaly detection
abstract: Current industrial anomaly detection models mainly employ either convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or Transformer networks in isolation, often overlooking their unique strengths and limitations in anomaly detection. This limits the capability of model to effectively handle diverse types of anomaly patterns. To this end, we propose a novel progressive framework for anomaly detection by strategically integrating these two architectures to leverage their respective advantages. First, we utilize the global receptive field and low-frequency information processing capability of the Transformer to restore the shape of input image. This restored shape information is then serves as auxiliary input to a CNN-based reconstructive module, enabling the subnetwork to perform a more refined reconstruction by relying on the structural context. Finally, by comparing the fully reconstructed image to the test image, we can accurately localize anomalous regions. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on industrial anomaly detection datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing anomaly detection across a variety of scenarios.

articleTitle: A current-constrained backstepping control method for LC-type three-phase inverters based on integral barrier Lyapunov functions
abstract: In this article, a current-constrained backstepping control method utilizing integral barrier Lyapunov functions is proposed for LC-type three-phase inverters. By introducing the integral barrier Lyapunov functions into the backstepping controller design, the inductor current-constrained problems of the LC-type three-phase inverter are transformed into the boundedness problems of the Lyapunov functions. On this basis, backstepping controllers are designed to ensure the boundedness of the Lyapunov functions, so that the output voltages of the inverter track the reference voltage while the inductor currents do not violate the constraints. The rigorous stability proof is given, and the effectiveness of the method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic adsorption wall climbing robot design with magnetic self-adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel wall-climbing robot with adjustable electromagnetic adhesion capabilities, which is capable of autonomously modulating its electromagnetic adhesion force in accordance with the current posture of the robot, thereby ensuring stable operation on surfaces with varying inclines. The robot's posture is detected by using an MPU6050 module, and precise posture solutions are obtained through the application of a Kalman filter. Subsequently, a mechanical analysis of the wall-climbing robot is conducted, followed by the construction of a mechanical model for the robot. Employing the COMSOL software suite, a finite element analysis of the electromagnetic module was conducted to scrutinize the factors influencing t he electromagnetic adhesion force. This analysis established the relationship between the robot's posture and the input voltage of the electromagnetic module. Subsequently, a prototype and an experimental testing platform were constructed to assess the wall-climbing robot's adhesion force. The experimental outcomes demonstrated that the robot functions effectively on walls inclined at various angles, with the electromagnetic adhesion force automatically adjusting in response to changes in posture.

articleTitle: Improving SimVP Model using Fourier transform and differential divergence regularization for better spatio-temporal prediction
abstract: In the realm of spatiotemporal image sequence prediction, the complexity of various models has incrementally risen in an effort to enhance prediction accuracy. Among these, SimVP adopts a distinctive approach by focusing on the simplification of the model structure while maintaining commendable predictive outcomes. SimVP is exclusively built upon CNN and eschews intricate advanced modules such as RNN, LSTM, and Transformer. However, models based on CNN might encounter limitations in managing long sequence predictions, as CNNs generally find it challenging to apprehend long-range temporal dependencies. Moreover, although SimVP exhibits robust performance on particular datasets, its generalizability has yet to be thoroughly substantiated, particularly when confronted with more intricate or varied data. In addressing these concerns, this paper presents an enhanced framework derived from SimVP, integrating a Fourier transform module within the model architecture to bolster its efficacy in handling data characterized by irregular shapes and subtle changing patterns. Additionally, this paper incorporates a differential scatter divergence regularization term during the model training phase to mitigate the issue of escalating frame-to-frame discrepancies when SimVP processes extended sequence data.

articleTitle: The reconstruction of radar reflectivity based on convolutional neural networks and Himawari-8 satellite
abstract: Meteorological radar data play a crucial role in monitoring severe convective weather. Radar reflectivity (RR) exceeding 35 dBZ typically indicates the presence of intense convective systems, which can impact various human activities, including aviation. Timely detection of such weather systems is essential for saving lives and protecting property. However, the spatial coverage of radars is limited over oceans and mountainous regions, significantly restricting their effective application. In recent years, the continuous advancement of deep learning technologies has enabled the extraction of hidden feature information, which has been increasingly applied to the study of various nonlinear processes. In this study, we develop a radar reconstruction network framework based on Fourier convolution and convolutional neural networks, designed to process multi-channel satellite data. We propose the Fourier Convolution-based Satellite Reflectivity Retrieval Network (FFC- SRRNET), utilizing multi-channel data from the Himawari-8 satellite to construct a dataset for training the radar retrieval model. To evaluate the performance of the proposed model, precipitation estimates generated by FFC-SRRNET are compared with those from other advanced deep learning models. The results demonstrate that the FFC-SRRNET model achieves superior radar reconstruction performance compared to models such as U-Net, Kans, and Mamba.

articleTitle: Model-free adaptive iterative learning heading control for unmanned surface vehicles with quantized information
abstract: This paper studies a model-free adaptive iterative learning heading control problem for unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) with quantized data. First, using the dynamic linearization technique and a redefined scheme, a compact form dynamic linearization model is established for USVs. Then, a logarithmic quantization mechanism is introduced to reduce the transmission burden, and a quantized model-free adaptive iterative learning control approach is designed. Ultimately, the convergence of heading control error of USVs governed by the proposed method is rigorously proved, and the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Trajectory planning control of 4-DOF tower crane based on differential flatness
abstract: Recently, tower cranes are widely used in the field of industry. How to achieve accurate positioning and payload swing suppression simultaneously is of great significance to improve production efficiency and reduce safety accidents. However, there are some defects in the existing trajectory planning methods, such as residual load swing and insufficient consideration of practical factors, which lead to difficulties in practical application. Therefore, a novel trajectory planning method of 4-DOF tower crane based on differential flatness is proposed in this paper. Firstly, two auxiliary signals are introduced to replac e the original state variables by differential flatness principle to simplify the control target. Then, the sixth-order triangular spline function is designed as the reference trajectory and the optimal transportation time is calculated. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed trajectory planning strategy can realize the accurate positioning of the trolley and the jib, improve the localization efficiency by 3.86% and 3.01% respectively and eliminate the payload residual swing to a large extent.

articleTitle: An effective atmospheric visibility forecasting model based on improved Rainformer
abstract: Visibility as a crucial factor in meteorology and transportation, significantly impacts human activities and safety. This paper achieves intelligent forecasting of atmospheric visibility by deep learning techniques, which enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of visibility predictions. Specifically, we propose a modified Rainformer model in conjunction with multi-source data fusion techniques. First, the hybrid approach is introduced to transform station-based data into gridded images. Next, attention mechanism based fusion block and weighted losses are designed to enhance the prediction accuracy of atmospheric visibility in China. The experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms typical models across multiple meteorological evaluation metrics. Particularly for predictions of extremely low visibility, the important CSI have improved by more than 20% compared with TrajGRU, underscoring its effectiveness and potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: Image denoising technique based on an improved lion swarm optimization
abstract: Image denoising is a basic and very critical technology in the field of image processing, which has always been a difficult problem in the field of image processing. Traditional image denoising recovery methods have two methods: spatial domain filtering and frequency domain filtering. Spatial domain filtering is accomplished by convolution of image signal and filter function. In many cases, templates can be used. The different filter functions get different templates, such as mean filter, median filter, etc.; the frequency domain filtering is accomplished by multiplying the frequency domain signal with the transfer function in the frequency domain, and this process is processed by Fourier transform. The disadvantages of traditional methods either fail to denoise well or remove noise while losing a lot of detail. In this paper, we introduce an image denoising technique based on an improved lion swarm optimization . Based on the traditional lion swarm optimization , the Reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced, which takes the lion as the individual in the search space, and constantly improves its search strategy through learning and interaction, as the objective function in the way of minimizing noise and maintaining image details. The experimental results show that this technique can effectively remove different types of noise and retain more image details and texture features. Compared with the traditional lion swarm optimization, the reinforcement learning idea has better search efficiency and search quality. In conclusion, the reinforcement learning-based lion swarm optimization is a very promising technique for image denoising. It can effectively solve the image denoising problem, and can be applied to other image processing tasks.

articleTitle: Dual-channel image anomaly detection
abstract: Image anomaly detection focuses on identifying areas that deviate from normal patterns. The most commonly used networks usually follow an encoder-decoder architecture. These networks learn from normal training samples to predict masked information and use the reconstruction error related to the masked data as an abnormality score. However, previous approaches ignore that the size of surrounding areas required to reconstruct various anomalies are different. Small receptive fields lack a holistic understanding of shape and spatial relationships, while large receptive fields tend to involve more undesired information and be ill-suited for handling local structures and textures. Based on these insights, this paper proposes an edge guided anomaly detection method. Specifically, we first utilize an encoder-decoder network with residual block and large receptive field to achieve edge restoration. Then a shallow network with small receptive field is introduced to conduct edge guided image reconstruction. Finally, we learn a discriminative network to identify anomalies, leveraging both of structural and appearance discrepancies for more comprehensive and accurate detection. Experiments on the industrial inspection benchmark dataset demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Research on complex defect detection technology of PV modules based on a improved YOLOv5 algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based algorithm for the detection and localization of complex defects in photovoltaic (PV) modules, as well as the completion of a PV modules complex defect detection system. Firstly, to address the challenge of detecting multi-scale targets in PV modules defect datasets, a cascaded detection network model based on YOLOv5 was designed. This model leverages upstream and downstream processes, adopting a holistic detection strategy for the components to precisely identify and locate 11 typical defects in a phased manner. Experimental results demonstrate that the cascaded model exhibits superior detection performance compared to traditional detection models, and maintains a relatively fast processing speed. Secondly, to address the shortcomings of the YOLOv5 algorithm in detecting tiny targets, an improved algorithm based on the Normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance (NWD) was devised. Experimental results indicate that this enhancement reduces sensitivity to the positional deviations of tiny targets, thereby enhancing detection accuracy. Lastly, in order to test its performance, the improved YOLOv5 algorithm is applied to a PV modules complex defect detection system with PyQt5 framework, which integrates two modules: inspector management and complex defect detection.

articleTitle: MoB-NetV2-RVFL: diagnosis of coronavirus (COVID-19) from CT images via a deep learning architecture
abstract: Computer-aided diagnosis has emerged as a crucial trend in modern medicine. Recently, CT-based automatic detection algorithms for lung infectious diseases suffer from issues of low accuracy and complex architecture. In this paper, three MoB-NetV2 models (MoB-NetV2-SNN, MoB-NetV2-ELM, and MoB-NetV2-RVFL) for the detection of COVID-19 in CTs are proposed. the MoB-NetV2 model is proposed by inserting batch normalization layers between bottlenecks in MobileNetV2 and substituting the fully connected layer with the Net-1 model (SNN, ELM, RVFL), i.e. MoB-NetV2-SNN, MoB-NetV2-ELM, and MoB-NetV2-RVFL. After comparison, it is found that the proposed MoB-NetV2-RVFL achieves an average accuracy of 93.42% on a private dataset comprising of 2392 images, while t he precision is reached at 97.33%. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that our MoB-NetV2-RVFL outperforms other existing algorithms in the literature. High classification accuracy and precision and low computing amount are achieved, thereby enhancing the potential application of the model in the field of medical image-aided diagnosis of COVID-19 virus.

articleTitle: Second-order fixed-time consensus with communication range constraints using output feedback control
abstract: The paper considers the second-order consensus for multi-agent systems (MASs) with fixed-time (FixT) conver- gence rate and communication range constraints. The considered communication networks are suffered to the constraints of communication range among agents. To retain the connectivity of the communication network, a connectivity-preserving consensus protocol is proposed without the use of velocity measurement. Furthermore, the agents can achieve consensus no later than a certain time and the convergence time owns an upper bound unrelated to the initial states. Lastly, an illustrative simulation is included to confirm the convergence of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: SimVP-MM: multi-source fusion for intelligent short-term precipitation forecasting
abstract: Short-term precipitation forecasting is crucial in meteorology, significantly impacting disaster prevention and mitigation, agricultural production, and daily life. Artificial intelligence technologies can enhance the accuracy and timeliness of predictions by processing large amounts of meteorological data. Among these, SimVP achieves higher prediction accuracy than many models by using only Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), while avoiding complex modules and training strategies. Therefore, this paper proposes a prediction network based on the SimVP model, which integrates radar reflectivity and satellite cloud image data as input. To further improve the accuracy of precipitation forecasting, we introduce parallel attention mechanisms to extract temporal and spatial features. Experimental results show that the proposed SimVP-MM method not only enhances precipitation prediction accuracy but also enables the prediction of convective initiation, addressing the limitations of radar data input.

articleTitle: Research on trajectory planning and active obstacle avoidance algorithm of multi-degree-of-freedom manipulator
abstract: The robotic arm is a key component of industrial production, and is widely used in manufacturing fields such as handling, spraying, welding, and grinding. Traditional trajectory planning methods, especially optimization-based methods, often require large amounts of computational resources. For example, the RRT algorithm performs well in dealing with high-dimensional spaces and complex environments, but it also has some significant shortcomings. The first is poor path quality, and the paths generated by the RRT algorithm are often not optimal, and may contain unnecessary twists and redundancy. The main reason is the lack of goal orientation, the expansion process of the RRT algorithm is random, and the lack of clear goal orientation, which may lead to low efficiency of path exploration. Therefore, the purpose of this paper is to use the artificial potential field method to solve the above problems, guide the expansion direction of the RRT algorithm through the gravitational field of the artificial potential field method, and push the path away from the obstacle through the repulsion field, so that the safety is greatly increased.

articleTitle: Design and development of a blood sample preparation instrument
abstract: Manual involvement in blood sample preprocessing can lead to various human errors and random contamination. The blood sample preparation instrument adopts an automated approach to preprocess blood samples, completing the aliquoting of blood samples and the dispensing of reagents. This article discusses a blood sample preparation instrument Sanguinary Arrange Gear(SAG) based on a distributed design, introducing its overall structural design and logical design, and detailing the motor control module, process control module, and database module. Experimental results indicate that the blood sample preparation instrument based on a distributed design exhibits good reliability and can effectively achieve the preparatory processing of blood samples.

articleTitle: Event-triggered prescribed-performance adaptive control for a class of uncertain parameterized nonlinear systems
abstract: Ensuring guaranteed performance is crucial for enhancing the control effectiveness of nonlinear systems. In this work, we focus on a specific class of high-order nonlinear systems characterized by uncertainties and introduce a tracking prescribed-performance control strategy that incorporates an adaptive estimation law. By implementing both static and dynamic event-based triggering, we enable the sampling of the input signal. Additionally, we consolidate the bounded uncertain variables into newly defined vectors and develop an adaptive control approach to manage them. It is demonstrated that the tracking error converges asymptotically to zero and that all signals remain bounded while achieving guaranteed performance. Through comprehensive theoretical analysis and simulation experiments, we validate the proposed adaptive tracking event-based control strategy for realizing prescribed-performance control in high-order nonlinear systems, ensuring that the Zeno phenomenon is avoided.

articleTitle: HarmonyNav: robot navigation in human-robot coexistence environment considering group and pedestrian intentions
abstract: Service robots must navigate efficiently and harmoniously in human-robot coexistence environments. Previous studies often treated pedestrians as independent entities, ignoring human intentions and leading to group intersections and perfor- mance issues. We introduce HarmonyNav, a crowd navigation algorithm that enhances human-robot harmony. Our method uses Human-Robot Interaction sub-networks to account for indirect group impacts on pedestrians and predicts pedestrian trajectories to infer intentions. Employing proximal policy optimization (PPO) in reinforcement learning, we develop a harmonious navigation policy. In simulation experiments, our results show improved navigation performance, reducing group intersections and individual intrusions.

articleTitle: Anti-disturbance low speed regulation control of PMSMs using modified extended state observer based on rotor position
abstract: A modified extended state observer (ESO) based rotor position algorithm is proposed for improving low speed regulation control performance. The speed signal is often obtained by differentiating the position signal. However, the position signal of encoder with quantization errors results in crawling and shaking at low speeds. Considering quantization error as a type of noise limited their own accuracy, the environmental influences like mechanical vibration and electromagnetic interference also lead to noise in rotor position. The modified ESO method incorporated a Kalman filter (KF) is proposed to reduce the negative impact of noise. Due to differential amplification noise, the position signal is used instead of traditional speed signal for observers design because of its undesirable characteristics at low speed. The modified ESO based on rotor position is used to estimate both speed signal and disturbances to enhance the low speed performance in the presence of disturabances and measurement noise. The friction model is embedded for above integrated structure due to its nonliearity at low speeds. Considering the negative effects of measurement noise and disturbance at low speeds, it has verified that the proposed algorithm has better dynamic and steady-state performance and anti-disturbance ability through simulation.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of discrete platelet function tester control machine upgrade
abstract: This paper focuses on developing fundamental functional upgrades for control systems in control machines, detailing the design and implementation of motion control functions, CAN communication functions, and related auxiliary features. The purpose of the upgrade is to improve the stability, sensitivity and functionality of the machine.To achieve precise control of the rotary sample disk servo system, it delves into the design of the servo motor control framework, introducing a fuzzy PI controller to enhance performance. To ensure reliable communication, a practical application layer communication protocol for the CAN system is established, creating a robust communication process with safeguards. The paper also explores the design and implementation of essential auxiliary functions for advanced control machines. Finally, it tests these functions to confirm the feasibility of the proposed upgrades.

articleTitle: An novel open set health monitoring method for electromechanical equipment
abstract: With the increase of efficiency and quality requirements in industrial production, the health status monitoring and diagnosis of electromechanical equipment becomes particularly important. In this paper, an open-set recognition-based health monitoring method for electromechanical equipment is proposed to cope with the problem of unknown health status that may be encountered in real applications. This method is developed by constructing an open-set identification multi-task neural network (OMN) in order to improve the recognition of unknown faults. We improve the competitive overcomplete output layer (COOL) and introduce an open-set multitasking network-based health monitoring method that does not rely on cumbersome feature extraction operations and is capable of achieving high open-set diagnosis accuracy. The superiority and generalisation of the proposed model is demonstrated through experimental validation on the bearing dataset and the rolling pin wear dataset.

articleTitle: CISC: coding curvature and intensity relations for loop closure detection
abstract: Loop closure detection is a critical and challenging task in autonomous driving, especially in enclosed indoor environ- ments like underground parking garages. In these scenarios, the limitations of traditional open-source algorithms lead to reduced accuracy and reliability, which presents significant challenges in practical applications. This study addresses these issues by proposing an innovative loop detection method that enhances performance through the fusion of point cloud curvature and intensity similarity. First, we introduce a novel global descriptor that integrates both geometric and intensity features, providing a more comprehensive representation of the surrounding environment. Second, recognizing the sequential correlation between elements of the global descriptor, we improve the construction of the ring key and apply it to consistency verification, thereby significantly enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of loop detection. Compared to current state-of-the-art algorithm frameworks, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves higher accuracy, better recall rates, and faster processing speeds in enclosed indoor scenarios. The successful application of this method offers a viable solution to the challenges of loop detection in closed environments within autonomous driving systems, presenting significant potential for practical implementation.

articleTitle: Formative education of Artificial Intelligence for preschool children: challenges and methods
abstract: With the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI education is gradually being integrated into early childhood education, becoming a key component of educational innovation. This study explores AI-based early childhood education for preschool children, analyzing its current status, objectives, content, and practical approaches. The core goal of AI education for young children is to guide them in understanding basic concepts of intelligence through engaging, playful methods, while promoting the development of their comprehensive abilities, including social skills, emotional cognition, and teamwork. However, the implementation of AI-based education for preschool children faces several challenges. In promoting AI-based early education for preschool children, it is crucial to design scientifically grounded educational tools while enhancing the awareness of parents and educators. This ensures that children can be guided to use AI educational tools effectively, while preserving the benefits of traditional education.
